findings.description: N*N*sizeof(int) can overflow, causing a smaller-than-needed shared memory segment and subsequent out-of-bounds writes.
atoi allows negative, zero, or non-numeric input; no validation of range or reasonableness of N.
No limit on matrix size; a large N can exhaust memory.
Using 0666 for shmget exposes the segment to all users.
Shared memory is left globally attachable while in use.
Unchecked return value: malloc, fork, shmdt, and some syscalls are not checked for failure.
random seeding with time is predictable; not a crypto use here but worth noting.
